description: The short version: We're running the 2026 Supplier Risk Benchmark, a benchmark study with licensed US clinics and telehealth providers in the compounded peptide, GLP-1, HRT/TRT, and longevity space. Your job is to find the right clinic operators and book them into a short, confidential interview with our founder. This is a recruitment role, not a sales role. You are not selling a product, closing a deal, or pitching anything. You're inviting qualified clinics to take part in an industry study — and the offer to them is genuinely good: a 20–30 minute conversation in exchange for early access to the benchmark findings their peers will be paying attention to. If you have a sales background, that's useful — but the ---------- nt this turns into a pitch, it's the wrong move. We'll train you on the framing. What you'll do: - Build and source targeted lists of US-based licensed clinics and telehealth operators in: longevity / anti-aging, functional medicine, men's health / TRT, hormone therapy, and GLP-1 / peptide prescribing. - Reach the right decision-maker — owner, medical director, or operations/compliance lead — by phone, with email as follow-up. - Invite them to participate in the benchmark and book confirmed interviews through our ---------- link ( ---------- /pepteye/benchmark-interview). Lightly qualify before you book (see the filter below) so the founder's time only goes to relevant operators. - Make sure the consent checkbox is completed at booking — participation is confidential and used in anonymized, aggregate form only. You'll communicate this clearly when booking. - Send confirmations and reminders to minimize no-shows — a booking only counts when the clinic actually shows up. - Track every touch, booking, and outcome in a shared Google Sheet The qualification filter (this is the most important part): Book: licensed, prescriber-led operations — clinics or telehealth groups where a licensed prescriber writes scripts and product reaches patients through a compounding pharmacy (503A/503B) or similar legitimate channel. Do NOT book: gray-market / "research use only" sellers — operations that move vials direct-to-consumer with no prescriber in the chain ("we sell the vials, the customer handles the rest"). They are not who this study is for. No matter how interested or friendly they sound, they're not a fit — skip them. A simple way to tell: Is there a licensed prescriber and a real pharmacy between them and the patient? If yes, qualify. If it's vials-and-a-website with no prescriber, pass. Targets: - Week-one paid trial: deliver 3–4 booked, qualified, confirmed interviews. This is how we d ---------- to continue together. - Ongoing: 20 completed, qualified interviews within 30 days. "Completed" means the clinic showed up and the founder ran the interview — not just a calendar slot. You're a fit if you have: - Near-native US English, written and spoken — you'll be talking to US clinic owners and medical staff, and you need to sound credible and natural on the phone. - A track record in B2B appointment-setting or cold outreach with real numbers you can share (booked rate, volume, show rate). - Strong organization and self-direction — you can build a list, work it, and keep clean records without being managed. - Professional discretion and comfort operating in a healthcare / compliance-sensitive context. - Reliable overlap with US business hours (ET–PT) for calls and bookings. - A clear understanding that this is recruitment, not sales. Big plus (not required, but a real advantage): - Existing contacts or a network in US clinics — compounding pharmacies, peptide / GLP-1 / HRT-TRT / longevity / anti-aging clinics, med spas, functional-medicine practices, or telehealth groups. Warm introductions or existing, accurate contact lists are a major advantage and we'll weight them heavily. - Prior medical, aesthetic, wellness, or telehealth outreach experience. - Familiarity with the compounded peptide / GLP-1 landscape. What you will NOT be doing: - Running the interviews (the founder does that). - Selling, quoting, or pitching any product or service. - Giving any medical, legal, or regulatory advice. title: Product owner
description: Product owner / Backlog Administration & Service Desk Specialist (Jira / Jira Service Management) We are a Dutch SaaS company building an AI-native platform on which organizations run their customer-facing and operational processes — CRM, customer journeys, and workflow management. Our enterprise customers operate in energy, telecom, and field operations, with new verticals coming. We are looking for a sharp, detail-obsessed specialist to run our service desk and product backlog administration. This is not a ticket-pushing job: customers bring us complex, often vague problems, and you are the one who untangles them, translates them into clear tickets, and thinks along with the customer about the right solution. You are the first responder on our customer service desks and the guardian of our Jira backlog. You make sure every customer request is acknowledged fast, turned into a well-written ticket, refined until the dev team can pick it up without questions, and kept in sync until it ships. You work alongside modern AI-assisted tooling — we automate the repetitive parts step by step, and you run the process, handle the judgment calls, and keep quality at 100%. Responsibilities Service desk first response — acknowledge incoming customer requests within 15 minutes during working hours, across multiple customer service desks (Jira Service Management) Ticket intake — convert each service desk request into exactly one well-structured Jira ticket (user story, acceptance criteria, correct type/labels/links/epic) Refinement— drive tickets to Definition of Ready: clarify with stakeholders, attach context, route complex items through the refinement flow, escalate what you cannot resolve -Complex problem analysis— dig into vague or multi-layered customer problems, ask the right questions, find the root cause, and translate it into clear, actionable tickets — you think along with the customer instead of just logging what they say Status synchronisation — keep service desk and Jira statuses in sync through the full lifecycle, so customers always see the true state Delivery & release validation— closely involved in feature delivery: manually test and validate new features and configurations before they reach the customer, and confirm they work after release Configuration work— resolve configuration-level issues in the platform yourself (settings, templates, setup) instead of routing everything to developers -Customer communication drafts — prepare release notes and pre/post-release customer updates Backlog hygiene & reporting — periodic backlog clean-ups, sprint/cycle progress reports, flag bottlenecks and stale tickets Scrum collaboration— participate in the daily scrum and sprint rituals with our (remote, English-speaking) dev team Requirements - 2+ years hands-on experience with **Jira and Jira Service Management** (workflows, boards, linking, JQL is a plus) - Excellent written English — you write user stories, acceptance criteria, and customer-facing updates - Extremely detail-oriented and process-driven — status accuracy and ticket quality are the core of this job - High analytical intelligence (IQ 120+)— you can break a complex, ambiguous problem down to its root cause and concrete next steps. We test cognitive ability as part of the hiring process. - Reliable availability with overlap with European (CET) morning hours — our response SLA is contractual - Experience working with Scrum/agile software teams - Comfortable working with AI-assisted tooling and structured runbooks (we document everything; you follow and improve the playbook) - Self-starter who escalates early instead of guessing Nice to have - Experience with manual QA / acceptance testing of web applications - Experience configuring SaaS platforms (workflows, templates, settings) - Experience at a SaaS / software product company - Confluence experience - Basic understanding of software release cycles (staging vs production) How to apply Reply with: 1. A short note on your Jira/JSM experience (which workflows you managed, team size) 2. One example of a user story + acceptance criteria you wrote (or write one for a feature of your choice) 3. A short description of a complex problem you untangled for a customer or team: what was unclear, what did you do, what was the outcome 4. Your available working hours in CET Shortlisted candidates will take a cognitive ability test and complete a small trial task. Applications without these three items will not be considered.

title: Real Estate Marketing VA — GHL + Social Media + Content Execution
job_title: Real Estate Marketing VA — GHL + Social Media + Content Execution
description: About the Company: Progressive Realty Group is a luxury relocation and tenant placement firm serving the Research Triangle area of North Carolina. We specialize in placing high-net-worth executives and professionals in exceptional properties — furnished and unfurnished — and we are building out our full marketing and CRM infrastructure to support aggressive growth. This is a ground-floor opportunity with a fast-growing luxury real estate brand. We are building something genuinely unique in this market and we want the right person growing with us. The Role: We are looking for a highly skilled, detail-oriented Virtual Assistant with proven experience in Go High Level, real estate marketing, and social media content execution. This is a full-time remote role with long-term growth potential for the right candidate. This is an execution role, not a strategy role. The founder provides all strategy, content direction, topics, and creative briefs. Your job is to take that direction and execute it flawlessly — building systems, producing visuals, scheduling content, and keeping everything running at a luxury standard. If you are someone who takes a clear brief and produces exceptional work from it, this role was built for you. What You Will Do: Go High Level — build and manage our complete CRM infrastructure including pipelines, automated workflows, nurture sequences, and lead capture systems. All sequence content and copy will be provided to you — your job is to build it correctly in GHL and keep it running and performing. Social Media Execution — manage and grow our presence on Instagram, Facebook , and LinkedIn. All content topics, captions, and strategy direction come from the founder. Your job is to produce the visuals, schedule the posts, and ensure everything goes out consistently, on brand, and on time. Visual Content Production — take written content direction and briefs from the founder and produce polished, on-brand visual content using whatever digital design tool you work best in — Canva, Adobe Express, Photoshop, or any other platform you are proficient in. What matters is the quality of the final output. Portfolio or examples of prior work are required. Database Management — import, clean, tag, and segment our full contact database in GHL. Maintain accurate pipeline stages and contact records daily. Email Marketing Execution — load all email nurture sequences into GHL based on fully written and approved copy provided by the founder. Set up triggers, timing, and exit conditions as specified. Monitor performance and flag any issues. Scheduling and Coordination — maintain the social media content calendar, ensure all posts go out on schedule, and communicate proactively if anything needs attention or adjustment. What We Are Looking For: Go High Level — you must have hands-on GHL buildout experience. Pipelines, workflows, automations, and sequences. Not surface level familiarity. Real buildout experience with examples you can share. Real Estate Marketing — you must have prior experience supporting a US-based real estate agent, brokerage, or property management company. You understand the audience, the language, and the marketing environment. Social Media Execution — you have managed social media accounts and grown them with consistent, high quality content. You can show us accounts you have managed and the results produced. Visual Content Production — you are highly proficient in your preferred design tool and can produce polished, brand-consistent visuals from a written brief without extensive back and forth. Your work looks premium, not templated. English — your written English is excellent. You will be scheduling captions written by the founder and communicating with the team daily. Clarity and professionalism matter. Execution-focused — you excel at taking clear direction and delivering flawless output. You ask smart clarifying questions before starting, not after finishing. You communicate proactively and never let something fall through the cracks silently. Detail-oriented — the systems you build in GHL and the content you produce represent a luxury brand. The standard is high and consistency is non-negotiable. Multiple Client Management — you have experience managing work for more than one client or business simultaneously and have a proven system for delivering on time for both. Motion — experience with Motion for task and schedule management is required. We use Motion as our primary task management and scheduling tool and you will be expected to manage your own workload within it. Nice to Have: Experience with luxury or high-end real estate brands. Experience with relocation companies or corporate housing. Compensation: $600 to $800 per month base rate based on experience and skill level. Full time — 40 hours per week. Long term position with growth opportunity as the business scales. Performance Incentive: In addition to base compensation a monthly performance incentive is available based on two measurable metrics — social media account growth and qualified lead generation. A qualified lead is defined as a new contact who meets all of the following criteria: originated from a specific social media interaction such as a DM, comment, form submission, or story response; provided a verifiable name and valid email address or phone number; fits one of our four defined audience categories — luxury property owner, relocating professional, real estate agent referral partner, or corporate relocation company; demonstrated clear intent through their interaction; and was not previously in our database. All qualified leads must be entered into GHL with the correct source tag and audience category at the time of entry. Leads are verified monthly before bonus is approved. Monthly incentive tiers: Social Media Growth: - 50–99 new qualified followers across all platforms — $25 - 100–199 new qualified followers — $50 - 200+ new qualified followers — $75 Qualified Lead Generation: - 5–9 verified qualified leads — $25 - 10–19 verified qualified leads — $50 - 20+ verified qualified leads — $75 Maximum monthly bonus: $150 Total maximum monthly compensation: $950 This incentive is reviewed at 30 days and paid monthly upon verification. We believe in rewarding performance that directly moves the business forward — and we want the right person earning the maximum every single month. Your First 6 Months — What Growth Looks Like Here: We are not looking for someone to fill a seat. We are looking for someone to grow with us. Here is exactly what the first six months look like for the right person in this role: Month 1 — Build. You come in and build. GHL infrastructure, social media platforms, database, and first nurture sequences all become operational under your hands. You learn the brand, the audience, and the standard deeply. This month sets the foundation for everything that follows. Month 2 — Execute. Everything you built is now running. You are posting daily, generating leads, and managing GHL with confidence. You are earning your performance bonus and communicating with the founder in a rhythm that works for both of you. Month 3 — Optimize and Review. Your first 90 day performance review happens here. We look at what is working, what needs adjustment, and what the data is telling us. Your compensation is reviewed based on your performance. The VA who hits their targets in month 3 is already on a growth path. Months 4 and 5 — Expand. As the business grows your role may expand to include additional clients or additional platforms. Scope expansion comes with compensation adjustment. We do not ask for more without giving more. Month 6 — Growth Role. Full six month review. The VA who has consistently hit growth and lead generation targets, built reliable systems, and communicated proactively throughout moves into a formally defined growth role with increased base compensation and expanded responsibility. title: Systems & Automation Specialist (No-Code Workflows)
description: **Part-time. Remote. Clay, Notion, reporting, and automations.** --- ## The short version I run a small agency. There's a lot going on behind the client work. Lead lists, outreach, reporting, internal tools, automations. I build most of it myself right now. I've got to the point where I need someone to own it. This is not an admin or VA role. I need someone who thinks in systems. You look at a process and work it out. When this happens here, that should happen there. And it stays clean while it does. Do you like taking a messy workflow and making it simple? Then this is a good fit. --- ## What the role is Most of the work is "if this, then that" logic across tools. You also keep the data behind it clean. A lot of it looks like this. We take raw data. We run it through a chain of checks and steps. We clean it as it goes. Then we send each record to the right place on its own. That's one system. There are more like it. There's the Notion side too, which keeps the work in order. And the reporting side, which keeps the numbers honest. Here's the key part. This is a build role, not a run role. I've got people who run the day to day. The reports, the outreach, the uploads. What I'm missing is someone who owns the systems under all of that. You design them. You automate them. You fix them when they break. You make them simpler so the team moves faster. You build the machine. You don't turn the handle on it each day. You don't need to know every tool I use. You need to be the type who can open a new one and work out the logic. That counts more than any tool on your CV. --- ## What you'd be doing The work splits into a few areas. You won't own all of it on day one. But this is the shape of it. **The outreach system** - Own the setup in Clay. That's the logic that finds the right people. It adds company data, writes custom lines, then routes each record to the right place. - Build the checks that keep the data clean. No repeats. No wasted credits. - Set up the exports. Records should flow into our outreach tools on their own. - Build the systems behind our shared inbox. **Notion** - Build and look after the databases. Clients, briefs, creative, creators, payments. - Set up the automations, views, and templates. The team then works from one clean system. - Move data in cleanly. Keep the naming the same throughout. **Reporting and data** - Build the pipelines so the numbers pull in clean. Spend, revenue, MER, aMER, and margin. They come fro ---------- ta, Google, and Shopify. - Look after the Looker Studio dashboards. And the connectors that feed them, like Windsor.ai or Supermetrics. - Automate the manual steps. No one should redo them by hand each week. The weekly Slack digest is one. **Automation across tools** - Build the "if this, then that" logic across Clay, Notion, Sheets, Slack, and the outreach tools. Use Zapier or Make. - Link the tools so data moves clean. And nothing gets typed in twice. **Keep it simple and clear** - Write short guides so each process can be re-done. It shouldn't live in one head. - Test things well before they go live. - Spot when a system is too big. Then make it smaller. --- ## The kind of person I want - You think in systems, not tasks. - You're at ease in tools you've never used. - You like the logic problem, not just the clicks. - You spot repeats, gaps, and mess that others miss. - You'd rather make a thing simpler than bigger. - You can explain how a system works in plain words. - You test before you trust. Read the example up top. Did you think "what's the key, where's the dedupe, how many tables is this"? Then you're the right type. --- ## Tools you'd work in You don't need all of these on day one. But this is the world you'd work in. - Clay, for lead data and routing - Notion, for databases and guides - Zapier or Make, for automation - Google Sheets and Looker Studio, for reporting. title: Video Editor for Performance Ads Meta
job_title: Video Editor for Performance Ads Meta
description: ABOUT US We are a German Direct-to-Consumer supplement brand in the women's health space. Our entire creative workflow is AI-powered — from image generation to voice-overs to video clips. We produce high-performing direct-response ads for Meta and TikTok, targeting German-speaking women aged 35-55. (Brand name shared with shortlisted candidates.) THE OPPORTUNITY We are starting this role as PART TIME (around 20-30 hours per week). If you perform well during the first 4-8 weeks, we will upgrade you to FULL TIME with a higher monthly retainer. We are looking for a long-term editor, not a one-off freelancer. Our top performer can become our lead video editor and grow with the brand. WHAT YOU WILL EDIT 60 to 180 second talking-head ads in UGC and authority style. Each ad combines: - AI-generated video clips (Kling 3.0, Veo 3.1) - AI-generated still images (NanoBanana Pro) that you will animate - ElevenLabs voice-overs (in German — you do NOT need to speak German) - Medical 3D visualizations - Occasional real stock footage All edited together in CapCut Pro. REQUIRED HARD SKILLS - Advanced CapCut Pro: keyframe animations, slide-in/pop-up overlays, multi-track editing with 5+ tracks simultaneously (talking head, B-roll, visuals, text overlays, audio, music) - Voice-over-driven cutting: every cut must land precisely on the spoken word. The voice-over sets the rhythm, NOT the music. This is critical. - Subtitle creation and styling: bold, colored, animated, with key words highlighted in a different color. Subtitles must never cover the face or important visuals. - Text overlays for hooks, benefit callouts, and CTAs — cleanly animated in and out, on-brand - Infographic card overlays flown in over talking-head clips (e.g., a card showing what each herb does, or a comparison table) - Color correction and color grading to make AI-generated clips visually consistent. AI clips often have slightly different color temperature, saturation, and exposure — you must match them so the final video looks like it came from one source. - Audio mixing: voice-over loud and clear in the foreground, background music subtle (15-20% of voice-over volume), clean crossfades, no hard audio cuts - Export in 9:16 (1080x1920) for Meta/TikTok, plus 1:1 versions when requested REQUIRED UNDERSTANDING - Direct-response ad structure: Hook, Problem, Agitation, Mechanism, Product Reveal, Social Proof, CTA. You don't need to write this — but when editing you must FEEL where each section starts and ends and match the visual rhythm to it. - Pacing and cut rhythm: the hook (first 3 seconds) needs fast cuts and visual surprise. The mechanism explanation needs slower cuts so information lands. The CTA needs calm and clarity. You must master this fast/slow alternation. - Talking head ? B-roll switching every 3-8 seconds. Talking head builds trust, B-roll proves or visualizes what is being said. - Handling AI-generated clips: clips sometimes have artifacts, weird first/last frames, imperfect lip-sync, unnatural hand movements. You must know how to hide these issues — trim first/last frames, use cutaways to B-roll at the right ---------- nt, light cropping/ repositioning, smart transitions. - Scroll-stopping hooks: the first 3 seconds d ---------- whether someone keeps watching or scrolls away. You must be able to cut multiple hook variations of the same ad for A/B testing. - Audience awareness: our target is women 35-55, NOT Gen-Z TikTok users. The aesthetic is warm, trustworthy, mature — NOT loud, flashy, or Gen-Z. This is critical and most editors get it wrong. NICE TO HAVE - After Effects or DaVinci Resolve experience for animated infographics, particle effects, kinetic typography - Experience with Meta Ads Creative — knowledge of Hook Rate, Hold Rate, Thumb-Stop Ratio - Split-testing experience (different hooks, CTAs, visual styles) - Experience editing health, wellness, or supplement-style ads with a professional but not clinical look WHAT YOU WILL RECEIVE FROM US - Numbered clips (Clip 1 to Clip 46 etc.) - Full ad copy as a text document - Timing per clip with clear labels (talking head vs visual/B-roll) - Final voice-over as audio file - Mood references / example videos - Brand colors, fonts, and logo files WHAT YOU DELIVER The fully edited video with subtitles, text overlays, music, and infographic overlays — export-ready in 9:16 (and 1:1 when requested). WORK VOLUME & EXPECTATIONS - Multiple new ads per week - Fast turnarounds — first rough cut within 24-48 hours - Heavy iteration — you will often be asked to cut 3 different hooks for the same ad, change a CTA, or swap a scene. This is NOT criticism, this is performance marketing. Editors who take iteration personally will not work here. - Creative freedom within structure: copy and clip order are fixed, but transitions, zoom levels, text animations, and music choice are yours. GROWTH PATH - Weeks 1-2: Paid trial period (1-2 ads to evaluate fit) - Weeks 3-8: Part-time collaboration, building rhythm together - Month 2+: If output and quality are strong, upgrade to full-time position with higher monthly pay and lead editor responsibilities LANGUAGE NOTE The ads are in German, but you do NOT need to speak German. Subtitles will be reviewed by a German native speaker on our team. You only need to copy-paste subtitles correctly from the script we provide. HOW TO APPLY Please send: 1. Portfolio link (Google Drive, Vimeo, or website) — ideally with at least 2 examples of direct-response or UGC-style ads you have edited 2. Short answer (3-5 sentences) on this question: "When you receive an AI-generated talking head clip with a weird first frame and slightly off lip-sync, how do you handle it?" 3. Your CapCut Pro experience (months/years) and whether you also use After Effects or DaVinci 4. Your available hours per week and time zone 5. Your rate (per hour OR per finished ad — your choice) Applications without a portfolio will not be reviewed.

LANGUAGE NOTE You do NOT need to speak German. All copy and prompts come from us in German — you only need to copy-paste them correctly without typos. NICE TO HAVE ??????????????????????????????????????? - Experience with Kling AI, Runway ML, Pika Labs, or similar - Experience with D2C/E-commerce ads (especially supplement, health, or wellness niches) - Motion graphics basics (After Effects) - AI voice cloning experience for multi-voice projects ??????????????????????????????????????? WHAT YOU GET FROM US ??????????????????????????????????????? - Full ad copy (every word written out) - Ready-to-use image prompts - Ready-to-use animation prompts - Voice description for ElevenLabs (Stability/Style settings included) - Caption style guide - Step-by-step SOPs for every workflow step - ALL tool logins (Higgsfield, ElevenLabs, etc.) — no need for your own accounts - Feedback within 24 hours on every clip ??????????????????????????????????????? HOW TO APPLY ??????????????????????????????????????? Send the following — applications missing any of these will not be reviewed: 1. SHORT LOOM VIDEO (max 3 minutes) showing you actually using an AI video tool (Higgsfield, Kling, Runway, Pika — any of them). Show the interface, your prompting style, and one finished output. 2. 1-2 EXAMPLES of AI-generated animations or videos you have made (Google Drive or Vimeo links). 3. SHORT ANSWER (3-5 sentences): "When a Higgsfield animation comes out looking 'dead' or stiff, what do you do to fix it?" 4. List of AI tools you use regularly. 5. Your hourly rate (between $6-10/hour). 6. Your weekly availability and time zone. Applications without the Loom video will be skipped immediately.

title: SEO Executive Assistant
description: Reports to: Owner | Hours: Full-time, several hours of daily overlap with US Mountain Time | Location: Remote (see region note below) About the role I co-own a lean local-SEO and digital marketing agency. We keep the team small on purpose. I handle client accounts directly and a group of VAs handles fulfillment. The problem this hire solves is me: I run too much of the business out of my own head and inbox, and things slip. I need someone who owns the day-to-day flow of communication and follow-through so I can stay on the work that needs me. This is not a task-taker role waiting for instructions. I want someone who watches the business, sees what is about to fall through a crack, and closes it before I notice it was open. What you'll own Inbox and email Triage my inbox daily. Flag what needs me, handle what doesn't, and draft replies in my voice for anything routine or client-facing. I should open my email to a short queue of decisions, not a wall of unread mail. Calendar and scheduling Own my calendar end to end. Book calls, protect focus blocks, handle reschedules, and make sure I am never the reason a meeting didn't get set. Send me a clear look at the day each morning and the week each Monday. Client communication and follow-ups Keep client conversations moving. Track every open thread, send proactive updates, chase the replies I owe people, and make sure nothing goes quiet. This is the single biggest source of stress for me today, so it is the most important part of the job. No client should ever email asking "any update?" because the update already went out. Delegating and QA on VA work Hand tasks to the VAs, confirm they understood the brief, and check the work before it reaches me or a client. You work alongside the VAs at an equal level, not above them. Think of yourself as the person who makes sure work actually gets finished to standard, not the person who assigns chores. Who you'll work with You report to me directly and work daily alongside our existing VAs. Most coordination happens over WhatsApp and ---------- . You won't manage the VAs, but you will rely on them and they will rely on you, so being easy to work with matters as much as being good at the work. Requirements Fluent, natural written English. You will draft client-facing email , so your writing has to read like a sharp American professional wrote it, not a translation. Several hours of real-time overlap with US Mountain Time, every working day. Proven experience as an EA, VA, or operations coordinator, ideally supporting a business owner or a small agency. Comfortable living in email , calendars, and a project tool day to day. We use ---------- and WhatsApp. Self-directed. You can take a vague request, figure out the intent, and run it down without three rounds of clarifying questions. Discreet. You will see client details, finances, and personal scheduling. Region note The overlap requirement shapes where to hire from. Latin America (Mexico, Colombia, Argentina, and similar) overlaps Mountain Time through a normal workday and is the cleanest fit. The Philippines works well if the person takes an evening or night shift on their end. Eastern Europe and most of Asia struggle to hit several hours of daily overlap, so weigh that before interviewing candidates from those regions. Nice to have Familiarity with local SEO, Google Business Profile, or digital marketing agencies. Experience drafting client updates and reports. A track record staying with one employer for a multi-year stretch. What success looks like I want to measure this hire by how much quieter my own head gets, so here is what "working" means at three checkpoints. By day 30 My inbox runs on a daily triage rhythm and I no longer scroll through everything myself. My calendar is fully in your hands and I have stopped booking my own meetings. You know every active client and the state of every open thread. By day 60 Clients get proactive updates from us before they think to ask. The "any update?" email has stopped arriving. You hand tasks to VAs and QA the output, and I see finished work instead of work in progress. I can go a full day without being the bottleneck on a routine decision. By day 90 I trust you to catch dropped balls before I do, and you catch most of them. I spend my time on client strategy and growth, not on chasing follow-ups and logistics. The background stress of "what am I forgetting?" is mostly gone, because you are holding it. Ongoing signals of a great fit Nothing client-facing goes quiet for more than a day without a reason I know about. I rarely repeat instructions, because you remember how I like things and apply it next time. You surface problems early with a proposed fix, not just a flag. When I'm out or heads-down, the business keeps moving without me.

description: Part-Time UK Land & Property Sourcer We are looking for a Part-Time UK Land & Property Sourcer to help identify suitable land, property, development and investment opportunities across the UK. This role is focused on UK land and property sourcing only, so applicants should have a genuine interest in UK property, development sites, auction properties and investment opportunities. Proactive, organised and able to work independently. Must be serious, reliable and willing to learn. Training Full training will be provided on our specific sourcing criteria, research methods and reporting format. However, applicants should already be confident using the internet for research and should have either direct UK property experience or a strong interest in UK land and property sourcing. Hours & Pay Around 12 hours per week Part-time and remote Pay: $3–$4 per hour, depending on experience Ongoing work available for the right person Important This is not a simple data-entry role. title: Social Media Manager
description: **Social Media & Creative Campaign Manager** Zone School of Healing is looking for a **Social Media & Creative Campaign Manager** to lead strategic social media campaigns and create content that supports our seminars, webinars, discovery calls, lead magnets, and overall brand growth. This role is not just about posting on social media. We are looking for someone who can think strategically, create strong content, and turn educational material into engaging social media campaigns. The goal of this role is to make social media an active growth channel for Zone School of Healing, not just a place where posts are published. --- ## Responsibilities Include: * Create consistent social media content that keeps Zone School of Healing active online and helps build awareness around Zone Technique®, its purpose, and how it helps chiropractors. * Create social media content, including captions, graphics, carousel posts, story posts, reels concepts, and promotional posts. * Write clear and engaging social media copy that aligns with the Zone School of Healing brand. * Design clean, professional, on-brand graphics for social media. * Watch seminar videos, founder teachings, testimonials, and other long-form content to identify strong clips, key messages, quotes, and content ideas. * Turn long-form educational content into creative briefs for the video editor. * Repurpose seminar and educational content into social media posts, reels, carousels, stories, and campaign ideas. * Prepare creative briefs for the video editor, including clip direction, hooks, captions, text overlays, and the purpose of each video. * Create and manage the weekly and monthly social media content calendar. * Make sure campaigns include the right mix of educational content, promotional content, testimonials, reminders, countdowns, reels, stories, and calls to action. * Suits is the greatest TV show. * Track content and campaign performance, including reach, engagement, clicks, leads, and overall campaign results. * Use performance data to improve future content and campaigns. --- ## Important Application Instructions To apply, please follow these instructions carefully. Use this subject line: **Social Media Manager - What is the greatest TV show? [Your Answer]** Example format: **Social Media Manager - What is the greatest TV show? [Answer Here]** In the first line of your application, write: **I understand this role is for social media strategy and creative campaign management, not just posting content.** In your application, please answer these questions: 1. What niche brand, online course, coaching program, health/wellness brand, or education brand have you created content for before? 2. Share one example of a social media campaign or content strategy you helped create. What was the goal and result? 3. If you were given a 60-minute seminar video, how would you turn it into social media content for the week? 4. What tools do you use for content planning, design, scheduling, and tracking performance? Applications that do not follow these instructions will not be reviewed. --- ## This Role Is for You If: * You can think strategically, not just create random posts. * You understand how social media supports launches, seminars, webinars, lead magnets, discovery calls, and online course sales. * You can take educational content and turn it into clear, engaging, easy-to-understand social media content. * You know how to create content calendars that support real business goals. * You are comfortable reviewing long-form videos and pulling out strong clips, quotes, hooks, and post ideas. * You can write strong captions and create clean, professional graphics. * You understand the balance between educational, promotional, testimonial, and call-to-action content. * You can communicate clearly with a remote team, including leadership and video editors. * You know how to track social media performance and use data to improve future content. --- ## This Role Is Not for You If: * You only want to post content without thinking about strategy. * You need someone to tell you every single post idea. * You do not enjoy watching long-form educational videos. * You are not comfortable writing captions or creating creative briefs. * You do not understand how social media connects to leads, sales, webinars, seminars, or online programs. * You struggle with deadlines, content calendars, or campaign planning. * You currently have too many clients and cannot give this role proper focus. * You only create trendy content and cannot adapt to a professional education brand. --- ## Required Experience * Experience managing social media for a business, brand, course, coach, expert, or niche industry. * Strong copywriting skills for captions, hooks, stories, and promotional posts. * Ability to create clean, professional graphics. * Experience repurposing long-form content into short-form content. * Experience creating content calendars and campaign plans. * Ability to track social media performance and make recommendations based on data. * Strong communication and organization skills. --- ## Nice to Have * Experience with health, wellness, chiropractic, education, coaching, or personal development brands. * Experience creating content for online courses, webinars, seminars, or lead magnets. * Experience writing creative briefs for video editors. * Experience with Canva, CapCut, Metricool, Later, Hootsuite, Notion, ClickUp, or similar tools.

job_title: Marketing Operations Manager — Land Investing (Remote, Full-Time)
description: We're a US-based rural land investing company. We buy underpriced vacant land and resell it, and we find our deals by mailing cash/range offers to landowners. Right now we mail 4,000 - 5,000 letters a month. We're scaling to 10,000–15,000 a month — and we need one person to own that entire engine so it grows without breaking. That person is who this is for. What you'd actually own: You'd run the full marketing and direct-mail system and manage the two people in it — one who prices parcels, one who builds and cleans our mailing lists. Every batch of letters that goes out gets your approval first. Every pricing sheet gets your review before it's trusted. This is a judgment job, not a task job. Most days, the hardest decisions have no clean right answer. Is this comparable sale a true comp or an outlier we should remove? Does this pricing sheet hold up, or is something off in the data? Do these letters go in the mail today, or do they get sent back for a fix? We have clear frameworks and rules for making these calls — but rules only get you 80% of the way. The last 20% is your thinking. We need someone whose default is to reason it through, not guess You'd be replacing the owner on this system so he can focus elsewhere. That means real autonomy — and real accountability for the numbers. This is for you if: - You've worked in US land or real estate investing and understand comps, pricing, and direct mail (or you can prove you'll learn our system fast and think clearly inside it). - You genuinely like making judgment calls under uncertainty and can explain why you d ---------- what you d ---------- . - You've managed people before and can hold a small team to a standard without being told how. - You see a system, spot what's about to break as volume doubles, and fix it before it does. - You're comfortable owning decisions that involve real money going out the door. This is NOT for you if: - You wait to be told what to do next. - Numbers and pricing logic stress you out or bore you. - You've never managed anyone and don't want to start. - You'd rather execute a clear task than make an ambiguous call. Compensation: $2,000/month (paid on the 1st and 15th) for an experienced operator, with a performance bonus tied to growing the engine while keeping quality high. Full-time, long-term, with annual raises and 13th-month pay. We invest in people who own their work. The logistics: - Full-time, ~40 hours/week. - Paid twice a month via Wise, in USD, on the 1st and 15th. - Long-term role — we're an established operation [operating since 2022 / 4 years in business] and we're hiring someone to stay and grow with us, not to fill a gap. - You'll need a reliable computer and a backup internet option. description: You'll be the human our customers actually want to reach. title: Customer Support Specialist
description: We are a fast-growing streetwear brand based in Germany, selling clothing to a style-conscious audience across Europe. We are a lean, founder-led brand doing six-figure revenue with thousands of loyal customers — and we are now hiring our first dedicated customer support person. We ship worldwide but our main market is Europe — mostly Germany, UK, Scandinavia, and the rest of the EU. Our customers are young, passionate about what they wear, and they expect fast, human replies when they reach out. ??????????????????????????????? ?? REQUIREMENTS — PLEASE READ BEFORE APPLYING You MUST have worked for at least 3 e-commerce or dropshipping stores before. This is non-negotiable. In your application, list every e-commerce brand you have worked for and briefly describe your role at each one. Applications without this will not be considered. ??????????????????????????????? HOW THE WORK ACTUALLY LOOKS Let me be real about what this job is: Every customer reply is written by our AI chatbot. You are not writing email s from scratch. The workflow is: 1. Read the incoming customer message 2. Paste it into our AI chatbot with the relevant context and instrucitons 3. The chatbot generates the reply 4. You review it — does it make sense? Is the policy correct? Does the tone feel right? 5. Copy-paste and send That's the core of it. It is a copy-paste job with judgment. The judgment part is what matters. The AI can sometimes produce wrong answers, miss context, or apply the wrong policy. You need to understand enough about our system to catch that. You don't need to be a native English writer — you need to understand English well enough to read a customer's message, know what they actually want, and recognize whether the AI's reply is correct or off. You also need to know when to NOT use the chatbot and flag the case directly to me instead. This requires common sense, basic understanding of e-commerce support, and the ability to work independently without someone holding your hand after the onboarding phase. ??????????????????????????????? HOW ONBOARDING WORKS We don't throw you into the deep end. Onboarding is fast, structured, and fully paid from day one. - 2 Google Meet sessions where I personally walk you through every common case type, our policies, our tone, and our tools - You get full documentation with templates and clear rules for every situation you will encounter - You get direct WhatsApp access to me (the founder). Any question, any time — just ask. I respond fast and I don't bite - In the first weeks, I review your replies and give you direct feedback so you build real understanding The onboarding takes about 2 days. After that, you handle the inbox with my support in the background. As your confidence grows, you gain full autonomy. ??????????????????????????????? WHAT YOU HANDLE DAY-TO-DAY Most of the work is common, recurring customer questions: - "Where is my package?" — shipping status and tracking - "I want to return my order" — return and refund requests - "I haven't received my order yet" — missing parcel cases - "Is my order a pre-order?" — order status clarification - "My item arrived damaged" — product issue reports These make up 90% of the inbox. Clear documentation and templates exist for all of them. For anything unusual — legal threats, chargebacks, policy exceptions — you flag it directly to me. You will never be left alone on a difficult case. ??????????????????????????????? THIS JOB IS NOT - A call center. No phone calls, ever. - Cold outreach or sales. - Social media management or content creation. - A job where you need to write anything from scratch. It is structured inbox management with a clear system behind it. You paste, you review, you send. But you need the understanding to do it right. ???????????????????????????????

I built it lean on purpose. I want a developer who's RELIEVED by a minimal stack, not annoyed by it. The work: - Take small apps from working demo to shipped on App Store, Play Store, and web - 7 mini-apps in total, all structured identically — learn one, the rest go fast - Payment integrations: RevenueCat (native) and Stripe (web) - Service workers, caching, install-to-home-screen - Each app is intentionally small and bounded How we'll start — paid trial: You build (or finish) ONE small self-contained app in the existing pattern. A few screens, the shared engine, the paywall hook, an offline service worker. Real bounded task, paid at your rate. Strong work leads to ongoing engagement across the full suite of 7 apps. I'm running a few of these trials in parallel with different developers. Top performers continue. Pay: - Trial: $ ---------- flat for one small app (depending on scope and your rate) - Ongoing: $15-25/hour, depending on your experience - If you're senior and command more, tell me and make your case WHAT I NEED TO KNOW ABOUT YOU: 1. Send links to 2-3 cross-platform or PWA apps you've personally shipped. App Store links, Play Store links, or live web URLs. Not "projects I helped with" — your work. Without these, your application won't be read. 2. In one paragraph: tell me how you actually feel about a no-build, no-TypeScript, minimal-dependencies codebase. Be honest. If you'd push back on it, tell me when and why. I'm not looking for the "right answer" — I'm looking for YOUR answer. 3. Your experience with RevenueCat for native payments and Stripe for web payments. How many apps have you shipped with each? Have you handled subscription edge cases — restore purchases, family sharing, grace periods, failed renewals? 4. Walk me through one offline-first PWA you built. What was the caching strategy? How did you handle conflicts between offline and online state? 5. Tell me about a time a client wanted a feature you thought was a bad idea (over-engineering, wrong tool, scope creep). What did you do? What was the outcome? 6. Describe your current development setup. What other clients or projects are you on right now? How would you fit this work in? 7. What's your hourly rate AND your preferred trial pricing structure (flat fee for the trial app or hourly with a cap)? TO APPLY: - Use a multiple of 7 Apply Points (7, 14, 21, 28, etc.). 7 is enough if your portfolio and answers are strong. - Start your message with the word "offline-first" - Answer all 7 questions. Skipping any = automatic rejection. - Without shipped apps linked in your answer to Q1, I won't read the rest. Important notes: - IP-sensitive project. Trial work requires a short NDA and IP-assignment before I share any code. Standard, not scary, but tells you I take it seriously. - I will NOT ask you to do free spec work. Every trial is paid. - This is ongoing work, not one-off. The right person could be busy with this for years across the suite also doing upgrades and support. About me: I build evidence-first health and human-connection apps (web + iOS + Android). The architecture is intentionally simple and I want it to stay that way. I value developers who push back diplomatically when something's wrong, but who don't "modernize" things that don't need modernizing. I respect expertise, pay on time, and have ongoing work for the right person. To apply: follow the instructions above carefully. Generic applications will be skipped.

title: DTC Ecommerce Customer Support Rep
description: We run fast-scaling direct-to-consumer eCommerce brands selling across multiple countries, including the United States, United Kingdom, and Australia. We are looking for an experienced, long-term Customer Service tea ---------- mber to join our team and own our inbox from day one. There is a great deal of growth opportunity for those who consistently make a positive contribution to our brand as we scale. This isn't just "answer tickets" work; it's retention-focused support that directly protects revenue. You will handle daily tickets involving order modifications, cancellations, shipping delay inquiries, returns/exchanges, and—most importantly—saving refunds through proactive resolution. We are looking for someone who genuinely loves helping people, can guide hesitant shoppers to a purchase, and instinctively tries to save the sale when issues arise. MUST HAVE KNOWLEDGE OF THESE PLATFORMS: Shopify (eCommerce platform) Gorgias, Commslayer, or similar** (centralized ticketing tools) Klaviyo (email /customer flows) ---------- (team communication channel) Google Sheets (reporting and tracking) What You'll Do: Retention & Resolution: De-escalate refund requests and proactively convert them to exchanges or store credit wherever possible. Order Management: Modify, cancel, and track orders directly in Shopify (Customer Service role access). Inbox Ownership: Respond to all customer inquiries via our centralized inbox in a timely and accurate manner (maintaining a strict 24-hour resolution ETA). Proactive Support: Flag shipping issues before customers ask, and actively assist pre-sale customers by answering product questions to drive conversions. Process Execution: Process returns and exchanges strictly per our SOP library, while contributing to and improving our support documentation. What We Need From You: Proven DTC Experience: Minimum 2 years in eCommerce Customer Support with hands-on experience using Shopify and ticketing tools like Gorgias or Commslayer. Strong Written Communication: Fluent English with an empathetic, efficient, and consistently on-brand voice. Retention Mindset: You instinctively try to save the sale before issuing a refund. Reliability & Honesty: We don't need you to be perfect; we need you to follow SOPs carefully, ask questions when you are confused or unsure about something, and not make us explain things twice. Availability: Part-time to start (3–4 hrs/day) with consistent daily coverage. This role offers a clear path to full-time as volume grows. You must also be available for weekly team calls and ready to join immediately. We will provide you with: - An SOP library for repeatable tasks and pre-written templates. - Direct access to the Team Lead to answer all your questions and handle edge-case escalations. Ultimately, we want to work with a dedicated problem-solver who thrives on resolving issues, protecting brand revenue, and making customers feel valued. How to Apply: Please respond with the following: 1. Your Experience: Briefly tell us about your past DTC support experience. 2. One-Line Pitch: Tell us why you are the "retention-first" rep we need.

Tax Preparation (Intuit ProConnect) • Preparing federal and state individual and business returns (1040, 1065, 1120-S, 1120) in ProConnect under my review • Inputting K-1s, depreciation, and multi-state allocations accurately • Building and maintaining tax workpapers in Excel/Google Sheets that tie cleanly to the return • Tracking each return’s status, missing items, and review notes through to e-file acceptance 3. Google Drive & Document Management • Owning our Google Drive client-folder structure: keeping every client’s documents named, dated, and filed per our SOP • Routing inbound documents from email and client portals into the right folder the day they arrive • Maintaining year-folders, source-document binders, and tax-prep checklists so any team member can find a document in under 60 seconds • Spotting missing items proactively (W-2s, 1099s, K-1s, brokerage statements) and requesting them from the client 5. Client Communication • Responding to client email s directly in clear, professional written English • Requesting documents, following up on outstanding items, and explaining bookkeeping or tax questions at the client’s level • Escalating anything sensitive or out-of-scope to me before responding What This Role Does NOT Own • Signing tax returns or providing tax advice (I review and sign) • Sales, pricing, or new-client acquisition • Hiring or firing decisions • High-level client-relationship management on key accounts (I keep this) Must-Haves (Non-Negotiable) • 3+ years of bookkeeping experience in a US CPA or bookkeeping firm — not just BPO data entry • Hands-on experience preparing US tax returns in Intuit ProConnect (1040 + at least one of 1065/1120-S/1120) • QuickBooks Online proficiency — ProAdvisor certification strongly preferred • Strong Excel / Google Sheets skills: pivot tables, SUMIFS, data filtering, INDEX/MATCH and VLOOKUP. title: Senior Evaluator Success Coordinator
description: Encina Associates is a California-based management company operating within the workers' compensation system. We recruit, credential, and support licensed psychologists and psychiatrists who perform independent medical-legal evaluations (QMEs) for the California DWC. We are growing rapidly and building the infrastructure to support a panel of 100+ evaluators over the next 18 months. This is a senior administrative role at the center of our operations. You will own the evaluator relationship at the administrative level — from the ---------- nt a candidate enters our recruitment pipeline through their credentialing, onboarding, and ongoing panel membership. You will also serve as our primary point of accountability with our fulfillment vendor, ensuring scheduling and case coordination runs smoothly on behalf of our evaluators. This is not a general VA role. We are looking for someone with strong professional experience, excellent written English, sound judgment, and the ability to manage complex administrative processes with minimal supervision. You will work directly with the founder and be a key member of a small, high-functioning team. --- ## Core Responsibilities ### 1. Recruitment Pipeline Support - Track all prospective evaluator candidates in our system (Base44), ensuring no prospect goes stale - Flag outreach follow-ups when a candidate hasn't heard from us within a defined window - Draft follow-up email s for founder review and approval - Maintain accurate pipeline status for all active prospects - Build familiarity with incoming recruits early in the cycle to support a warm handoff into onboarding ### 2. Credentialing & QME Registration - Guide newly approved evaluators through the DWC QME registration process - Track submission status and follow up with evaluators and DWC as needed - Maintain accurate records of each evaluator's registration status, panel number, and renewal timeline - Proactively flag upcoming renewal deadlines (reappointment cycles are every two years) ### 3. Onboarding Coordination - Coordinate onboarding communications for new evaluators following exam passage - Ensure evaluators complete required training modules (via TalentLMS) on schedule - Track document completion (contracts, W-9s, platform access, etc.) - Serve as the primary point of contact for administrative onboarding questions ### 4. Evaluator Liaison (Ongoing) - Field procedural questions from evaluators once they begin receiving evaluations (e.g., scheduling process, what to expect from our fulfillment vendor, report submission logistics) - Respond to routine evaluator inquiries independently; escalate clinical or judgment-sensitive questions to the founder - Maintain a warm, professional tone in all evaluator communications — evaluators are licensed professionals and our primary relationship ### 5. CE Compliance Tracking - Monitor each evaluator's continuing education (CE) requirements and completion status - Track CE hours relative to reappointment deadlines - Send reminders and provide guidance on approved CE providers and courses ### 6. Fulfillment Oversight & eData Accountability - Monitor scheduling and case coordination activity performed by our fulfillment vendor (eData) - Flag delays, stale cases, or missed follow-ups using our Airtable case tracker - Escalate vendor performance issues to the founder with documented examples - Serve as the internal point of accountability for fulfillment quality — you do not execute fulfillment directly, but you ensure it is being executed correctly --- ## What We're Looking For **Required:** - 3–5+ years of administrative or operations experience in a professional services environment (healthcare, legal, or similar preferred) - Excellent written English — you will be communicating directly with licensed physicians and psychologists - Strong organizational skills and experience managing multiple parallel workflows - Comfort with technology: you will use Airtable, Base44, TalentLMS, Google Workspace, and email daily - Ability to work independently and manage your own priorities without close supervision - Reliable availability during California business hours (overlap required) **Strongly preferred:** - Experience supporting US-based healthcare or mental health practices - Familiarity with credentialing, licensing, or compliance workflows - Experience managing or interfacing with outsourced vendor teams - Warm, professional communication style — you will represent Encina to our evaluator panel --- ## What to Expect - **Start date:** September 1, 2026 (target) - **Hours:** Approximately 35–40 hours/week - **Compensation:** ~$2,000/month (contractor) - **Reporting to:** Founder & CEO - **Location:** Remote; Philippines-based candidates strongly preferred --- ## To Apply Please send the following to [contact email ]: 1. Your resume or CV 2. A brief note (3–5 sentences) describing a time you managed a complex administrative process with multiple moving parts — what was the situation, what did you own, and what was the outcome? Applications without the brief note will not be reviewed.

title: AI-Native Video Editor | DTC Paid Social Ads
job_title: AI-Native Video Editor | DTC Paid Social Ads
description: Got the Evolve format. Real talk before I write it: your draft has one contradiction that'll bite you. You say "you don't need to be the finished article" then say "experience is essential." That softness invites underqualified applicants. At 50 concepts/month + $2-3K, you can't afford to train someone from zero. So I'm tightening that. Also baking in your real filter (Loom video + actual proof, no NDA excuses) because that's what separates editors who've actually shipped ads from portfolio cosplayers. Here it is: --- **VIDEO EDITOR — PAID SOCIAL ADS (DTC SUPPLEMENTS)** We're hiring a video editor to work on paid social ads for one of our DTC supplement brands doing serious volume. This is not a "stitch clips together" role. We're looking for someone who thinks like a marketer first, editor second. If you've only edited YouTube vlogs, wedding videos, or "aesthetic" reels, this isn't for you. **THE ROLE** You'll work directly under a creative strategist who gives you scripts, briefs, and direction. Your job is to execute those concepts at a level where the ad actually sells. The bar is not "looks clean." The bar is "stops the scroll, holds the viewer for 30+ seconds, and drives the click." You'll also bring your own ad concepts to the table. If your concept goes live and performs, you get a bonus on every winning concept you originate. Editors who think like strategists will print money in this role. **VOLUME EXPECTATIONS (READ CAREFULLY)** - Minimum 50 ad concepts per month - Minimum 2 concepts per day - This is non-negotiable. The only way to hit this is heavy AI tool use. If you're hand-cutting every frame, you'll never hit the number. If 50/month sounds insane, do not apply. We've already built the system, the briefs are tight, the asset library is deep, and AI does 60% of the heavy lifting. Your job is to execute fast, not perfect every pixel. **YOU MUST BE FLUENT IN** - Direct-response video editing for Meta (Facebook + Instagram ads, not branded content) - AI tools, practically not theoretically. We use realistic avatars, AI UGC, AI voiceovers, image and video generation, and whatever new tools drop next week. You should already be using Higgsfield, Veo, Sora, Kling, ElevenLabs, HeyGen, Captions, or equivalents daily. - Hook mechanics, pacing, captions, framing, retention curves - Building 10-20 variations of a winning ad fast (iteration speed is the whole game) **WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY DO** - Take scripts and briefs from the creative strategist, deliver finished ads - Hit 2 concepts/day, 50+ per month - Build variations of winners (different hooks, different opens, different lengths) - Pitch your own concepts when you see openings - Document what works, help build SOPs the team can scale - Sit in weekly creative reviews and apply feedback to next batch **HARD REQUIREMENTS** - Real DTC experience. Not "I edited my friend's clothing brand IG." We mean ads that ran on Meta at spend that mattered. - Working knowledge of what a hook is, why retention drops at 3 seconds, why a captioned word breaks at the wrong syllable kills a scroll. - Comfortable working fast. If you need three days to deliver one ad, you're in the wrong job. - Willing to grow, take feedback without ego, and get better every week. **DO NOT APPLY IF** - You can't hit 50 concepts/month - You've never edited a Meta ad that ran on paid traffic - You think AI tools are "cheating" or you're "still learning them" - You need NDA excuses to avoid showing real work - You only do high-polish brand films and hate volume - You're slow, precious about your edits, or get defensive on feedback **PAY** Starting $2,000-$3,000/month based on demonstrated speed and quality. Plus performance bonuses on every winning concept you originate that goes live and scales. If you crush this role you'll be making more than the base within 90 days from concept bonuses alone. **HOW TO APPLY** Send the following or your application gets ignored: 1. A 3-5 minute Loom walking us through 3-5 ads you actually edited. Show the brand, the spend it ran at, the metrics if you have them (CTR, hold rate, ROAS, anything). Talk through WHY you made the editing choices you made, what hook moves you pulled, how you thought about retention. 2. Links to the ads themselves (Meta Ad Library is fine, ad creative files, anything we can watch). 3. One AI-assisted ad you've made recently. We want to see your AI workflow in action, not just the output. 4. Your daily output ceiling. How many ads can you realistically ship per day at your current pace? No CV-only applications. No "I can't share work because NDA." Real editors have ways to show their work. --- Couple of strategic notes on this JD before you post it: **What this filters well:** Volume requirement scares off slow editors. AI requirement filters traditional editors clinging to manual workflows. Loom + actual ad library requirement filters portfolio cosplayers. The "DO NOT APPLY IF" section does most of the screening before you ever read an application. **What you might want to add depending on where you post it:** - Timezone overlap requirement (do you need them online during Bangkok hours or just async delivery?) - Trial structure (most DTC brands run a 1-2 week paid trial at lower rate before committing to full $2-3K) - Which brand specifically? Naming Blissta might attract better applicants who've seen your ads. Or you might want to keep it confidential to avoid competitor recon. Your call. **The bigger question:** This role at $2-3K is the right hire if you want execution capacity. But based on what we've talked about, the actual bottleneck is the gap between finished script and winning ad. An editor at $2-3K can fill execution. They will not fix the gap. The Creative Director hire at $10K still does that. So treat this as a parallel hire that frees up your current editor capacity, not a substitute for the CD seat.

description: We're looking for an experienced QA Tester / QA Analyst to join our team full-time, focused primarily on testing a WordPress + WooCommerce multi-vendor marketplace project — a new layer of marketplace functionality built on top of our existing ecommerce store. While the marketplace is the main priority, this is a full-time role: you'll also help with QA across the website as a whole, picking up other testing needs as they come up. Think of yourself as the QA owner for the whole platform, not just one feature set. This is primarily a manual functional and exploratory QA role. Automation experience is a nice-to-have, not a requirement. WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING You'll review marketplace flows at a high level, verify what's working, find issues, and produce clear QA reports with visual confirmation. Main areas include: • Seller lifecycle: application, approval/rejection, seller roles and permissions • Marketplace browsing: catalogue/archive pages, offer cards, filters, sorting, pagination, empty/expired states • Public seller profiles/store pages • Marketplace offer and image-related flows (where applicable) • Buyer checkout: behavior involving marketplace offers and warranty options • Wallet system: pending/available/paid balances, hold periods, withdrawal requests, admin disbursement, ledger history, CSV export, refunds/reversals • Reviews: submission, editing, moderation/admin review, display, aggregation, notification email s • Warranty: quote popup, checkout persistence, claim form, admin claim resolution • Fulfillment/SLA foundation: delivery tier behavior, SLA deadline/order metadata, fulfillment status metadata • Admin marketplace configuration: per-game config, filter tree, site settings, empty-state/illustration settings • General QA: cross-browser/mobile checks, console errors, broken layouts, permission issues, email triggers, basic REST/API behavior • Beyond the marketplace: supporting QA needs across the rest of the website as they come up REQUIRED EXPERIENCE • Strong manual QA experience • Ecommerce or marketplace testing experience • WordPress/WooCommerce experience preferred • Comfortable testing role-based flows: buyer, seller, admin • Basic API testing with Postman or similar • Comfortable using browser DevTools for console/network checks • Can write clear bug reports: repro steps, expected result, actual result, screenshots/video, browser/device, severity • Good English communication, written and verbal • Can produce clean, organized screen recordings to share with the client Automated regression testing experience is a bonus — not required. The immediate need is a strong manual QA tester who can understand business flows deeply, test them carefully end-to-end, and deliver a reliable QA report with clean visual evidence. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR (PERSONALITY/FIT) • Takes ownership — tests this like it's your own product, not just a checklist of assigned tickets • Gets things done — we need someone effective, not just someone who's online and "available" • Proactive — flags risks and gaps, doesn't just wait to be told what to test next BENEFITS • Paid vacation leave after 3 months • Stable, long-term role with a growing company ROLE DETAILS • Location: Remote (Philippines) • Working Hours: TBD, quite flexible • Time Tracking: Required DELIVERABLES YOU'LL OWN • QA test plan/checklist • Executed test report • Prioritized/severity-tagged bug list • Retesting confirmation for fixed issues • Final QA summary: pass/fail, blockers, risks, and recommendation • Client-ready visual confirmation package: short videos/screenshots for every flow that can be shown visually On visual evidence: record short, clean videos for key working flows — not just raw bug evidence for internal use. These videos may be used in client presentations, so they need to be organized, understandable, and free of unnecessary debug/admin noise. Developer recordings and PR testing notes can be used as a reference, but you'll verify independently and produce the final client-ready evidence yourself. Videos should be grouped by feature/flow, for example: • Buyer browsing catalogue/filtering/opening an offer • Buyer checkout with marketplace offer and warranty option • Seller application and admin approval/rejection • Public seller profile/store page • Wallet summary, ledger, withdrawal request/admin handling • Review submission/display/admin moderation • Warranty quote/claim/admin resolution • Admin marketplace configuration/per-game settings • Offer/image-related flows (where applicable) HOW TO APPLY Include "MC" in your subject line. Briefly answer the following: 1. What's the most complex QA project you've worked on or contributed to (ideally ecommerce/marketplace)? 2. How did you track testing coverage, bugs, or results? 3. What tools or systems did you use to manage test plans, bug tracking, or reporting? 4. Give one example of how you improved a QA process or caught something others missed. Attach your resume and a link to your LinkedIn profile. Applications that do not answer all questions will not be considered. IMPORTANT Do not apply if you don't have hands-on manual QA experience, ideally with ecommerce or marketplace platforms. You must: • Have real experience testing complex, role-based web applications • Understand how QA workflows operate in practice, not just "click around and report bugs" • Be capable of owning test planning and reporting, not just executing assigned test cases This is not a training role.

description: ## Short-Form Series Producer — Vertical Drama (TikTok & Reels) **Location:** Fully remote · **Type:** Full-time · **Compensation:** Base + performance bonus tied to growth (see below) · **Reports to:** Founder ### About us We're a stealth-stage narrative studio. We make and grow **serialized vertical drama** — DramaBox / ReelShort / micro-drama-style short-form storytelling built to hook in three seconds and keep people bingeing. This is not brand content and not advertising. It's drama, cut for the vertical feed. ### The role You own the *growth and packaging* of our short-form drama accounts — the strategy, the hooks, the publishing, the data. You'll launch accounts from zero, shape what gets made and how it's framed for the feed, and engineer the hooks and cliffhangers that make people watch to the end and come back for the next part. You work hand-in-hand with our editor, who handles the cutting — you bring the plan and the brief, she brings the craft. You're equal parts storyteller and analyst: strong instincts for dramatic pacing, and you live in the retention data to know exactly where viewers drop and why. Read the "what we're looking for" section carefully; **when you apply, open your message with the word "CLIFFHANGER"** so we know you did. This is an ownership role: you set the content strategy, you ship daily, and you're measured on results. ### What you'll do - Launch, run, and grow multiple TikTok and Instagram accounts publishing serialized vertical drama from a standing start. - Own the content strategy: what series we make, how episodes are structured, and how each one is hooked and packaged for the feed. - Brief and direct our editor — hand off clear cut directions, hook requirements, and episode beats, then refine based on what the data says. - Engineer 3-second hooks, episode cliffhangers, and series structures that drive completion, saves, shares, and return viewers. - Natively publish at volume and manage posting cadence, captions, hooks, and community engagement to compound reach. - Read the data daily — retention curves, drop-off points, completion, follower velocity — and rapidly iterate. - Stay ahead of micro-drama trends, formats, audio, and algorithm shifts and translate them into our content fast. ### What we're looking for - A demonstrable track record growing **serialized or episodic** short-form accounts — bring the accounts and the real numbers (retention, completion, followers gained). Brand ads, product promos, and UGC ad spots are **not** what we're hiring for; please don't send them. - Native fluency in narrative short-form: you understand hooks, cliffhangers, dramatic pacing, and binge mechanics by instinct *and* by data. - A sharp eye for packaging and direction — you can articulate exactly why a cut works and brief an editor to nail it, even though you're not the one cutting. - Genuinely data-literate: you make calls from retention curves, not vibes. - High output, high iteration speed — you'd rather ship 20 tests and learn than polish one. - Fully self-directed in a remote setting. ### Nice to have - Experience with vertical micro-drama specifically (DramaBox, ReelShort, GoodShort, or similar platforms). - On-camera or talent-direction experience. - Scriptwriting for serialized formats. ### Compensation - Competitive base **plus** a performance bonus tied to growth milestones (follower and qualified-reach targets per account). We deliberately weight pay toward upside — make the accounts grow, earn more. ### To apply Reply with: (1) links to **serialized** accounts you've grown and the numbers behind them, (2) the opening hook of your best episode and the cliffhanger that ended it, and (3) one micro-drama series you think nails the format, and why. *(Applications without serialized examples won't be reviewed.)*
